summary: Both deep dives are now exceptional for a general-audience film, and they are in sync. AlexNet runs as a complete, checkable chain. A photo becomes 224×224×3 = 150,528 numbers (s03). A Sobel-style tin stencil gives a worked sum of -4, then RELU clips it to 0. The next position gives max(0, …) = 3.88, then the stencil slides into a convolution that lights the 4's outline (s04). Five stencil layers rise into edges, textures, parts and things, then two halls of 4,096 and 1,000 answers (s05). The stencils start as noise and are cut by the 1986 messenger (s06). The ReLU weir is drawn against the squashing sigmoid, with the 6× race (s07). The overfitting scale weighs 1.2M labels × 10 bits = 12M against 60M weights, and is answered by crops/mirrors ×2048 (s08) and dropout in fc6/fc7 (s08b). Then come the two-GPU colour split (s09), the learning rate cut three times in the fog (s10), and 15.3 vs 26.2 top-5 with the seven-net caveat. The transformer is just as rigorous. The bottleneck funnel is followed by the 2014 attention grid. Then comes the all-pairs hall on 'every'. Q/K/V cards grow on knobs. Then 'crossed the river bank' is worked out by hand: question 1201 · labels gives 2/0/4/2, ÷√4 gives 1/0/2/1, and softmax gives 0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20. I recomputed every value and all are correct. Next the unscaled 8/0/-8 → 1.00/0.00/0.00 freezes while ÷8 pours 0.67/0.24/0.09 (also correct), and the real formula softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V lands as the payoff. Then 8 heads × 64 numbers, sinusoidal clock-face positions, attention → feed-forward ×6, the n² cost, and the causal staircase mask for GPT. An expert will respect this. Because each step is a picture first and a symbol second, a 15-year-old can follow it. The era structure holds end to end. Every candle has a belief, a named dissenter at its rim and a duration. Most round-3 items are confirmed fixed on their sheets at the ledger's word times, including the three-round ch08-s05 regression and the ch10-s04 dark beat. What keeps clarity from 9 is a few unspoken jargon captions. In ch10-s12, 'one-seventh … GNMT+RL (derived)' came back under a new spelling after it was routed out. In ch10-s10 the caption reads 'untrained toy weights: real bindings'. The fast L0114 (221 wpm), the user's own turn into the story, works against comprehension right where a newcomer is getting their bearings.

issues.problem: This is marked fixed, but it is not (round-3 T303 / round-2 T207, fourth round). BLEU is gone. best_moments: ch10-s06 + ch10-s07: a complete attention computation a viewer can check with a pencil. Question × label gives 2/0/4/2, ÷√4 gives 1/0/2/1, and the softmax jug pours 0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20, so 'bank now means: water'. Then why halve: 8/0/-8 slams into one cup ('learning freezes') while ÷8 pours 0.67/0.24/0.09, landing on Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V. Every number is correct.

ch08-s04: the pierced tin stencil as a real edge kernel. (-1)(1)+(-2)(1)+(-1)(1) = -4 becomes 0 under RELU; the next position gives max(0, …) = 3.88 on 'nearly four'; then the slide lights the 4's outline on 'convolution'.
ch10-s04 (fixed): the slips glow faintly on 'attention', threads start on 'every', and every pair down the hall is joined by 'all at once'. Self-attention as a single unforgettable image.

ch08-s08: the overfitting argument as a balance scale. 1.2M labels × ≈10 bits = 12M answers against 60,000,000 weights, the OVERFITTING card, then 'crops and mirrors: ×2048' re-weighting it. Real AlexNet reasoning a teenager can follow.

ch08-s05 (fixed at last): the cathedral of five stencil courses lighting edges → textures → parts → things in the rose window, then '5 stencil layers → 2 great halls of 4,096 → 1,000 answers' beside '≈60 million numbers / 650,000 neurons'.

ch10-s14: decoder-only made visible. The encoder half is cut away ('Liu et al., Google · Jan 2018 / OpenAI GPT · June 2018'), then the dark staircase curtain masks the future, and the ghost slot appears on 'what comes next'.

ch05-s07 (fixed): MYCIN's blinded test (65% vs Stanford specialists 42.5-62.5%), 'never went into routine use', then Hubert Dreyfus named with his 1972 book, and his verbatim 'early, dramatic success followed by sudden unexpected difficulties' over a cascade of falling IF…THEN slips. Belief, evidence, dissent and pattern in 31 s.

ch04-s01: XOR on a square with an 'on the wrong side' counter. One cut leaves 1 or 2 wrong; then the hidden layer remaps the space so (0,1) and (1,0) fold into one point (×2) and a single cut leaves 0. That is the actual reason a hidden layer works.

ch07-s01: the 1995 bet resolved on cards. JACKEL: BY 2000, NETS EXPLAINED and VAPNIK: BY 2005, NETS UNUSED are each struck through, giving 'JACKEL, 2000: LOST / VAPNIK, 2005: LOST'. The user's 'who paid for dinner?' is answered legibly.
